title: Video Friday: Robot Decommissioning Takes a Fun Turn
summary: IEEE Spectrum’s Video Friday round-up highlights a grab bag of robotics demos, including Devanthro selling novelty plastic balls, Pollen’s ringtone-worthy robot audio, EPFL LMTS’s thread-like linear motor, and a KUKA robot-arm car wash that still seems rough in real-world reviews. The more research-heavy items include Workhorse, which learns contact-rich whole-body humanoid manipulation from robot-free human demonstrations and runs on a Unitree G1 to sort boxes, catch a thrown box, and climb over a suitcase; MIT’s SANDO navigation system, which replans collision-free paths around moving obstacles using onboard sensing with mathematical safety guarantees; and an NC State soft swimmer that uses only two pneumatic inputs to switch among jellyfish-like, fish-like, and rotor-like underwater motion.

extra.full_text: Video Friday is your weekly selection of awesome robotics videos, collected by your friends at IEEE Spectrum robotics. We also post a weekly calendar of upcoming robotics events for the next few months. Please send us your events for inclusion. CoRL 2026 : 9–12 November 2026, AUSTIN Humanoids 2026 : 6–9 December 2026, SANTA CLARA, CA Enjoy today’s videos! It’s possible that I wasn’t the only one who thought that Figure’s recent stunt was somewhat ridiculous. Devanthro is in fact selling these plastic balls for $1000 each, and they’ll arrive in time for Christmas. [ Devanthro ] Not that anyone uses ringtones anymore, but if we did, this would be absolutely everywhere and I’d be loving it. [ Pollen ] Let’s not get too excited, but this thread-like linear motor is pretty sweet. [ Ecole Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne LMTS ] What is this robot for? It’s for doing exactly what you see here, that’s what it’s for. [ RAI Institute ] Humanoid robots still struggle to plan contact-rich whole-body manipulation from egocentric RGB and proprioception. Workhorse learns such manipulation from robot-free human demonstrations. On a real Unitree G1, Workhorse sorts boxes with its hands and a kick, catches a thrown box, and topples and climbs a suitcase. Yeah that happens to me too when I have a communication failure. [ Hybrid Robotics ] A car wash that models your vehicle then cleans it with robot arms? Interesting idea. The recent reviews from this location suggest that the robots aren’t quite up to snuff yet, but really seems like there’s potential here. [ KUKA ] So this is not the worst idea I’ve ever seen for what to do with humanoid robots. [ DEEP Robotics ] Some lovely manipulation with a deceptively simple gripper. [ Generalist ] I am genuinely embarrassed to say that this robot dances better than I do. [ General Robotics Lab ] MIT researchers developed SANDO, a new navigation system that helps robots safely navigate unfamiliar environments while avoiding moving obstacles. The system can rapidly plan and adjust a collision-free path using onboard sensors and computing, with safety backed by mathematical guarantees. [ MIT News ] Can you spot the part of this video that I’m side eyeing? Yep, it’s where the middle clip starts after the hand already has a good grip on that peelable strip. [ Sanctuary AI ] Inspired by feather stars, the NC State researchers report a soft underwater swimming robot capable of achieving three distinct swimming modes—jellyfish-like vertical swimming, fish-like directional steering, and rotor-like 3D reorientation—using only two pneumatic inputs. [ NC State University ] Here’s a series of mini-keynotes from ICRA earlier this year, on manipulation, humaonids, and embodied design. [ ICRA 2026 ]

title: New York extends AI companion program in partnership with Intuition Robotics
summary: New York’s Office for the Aging is extending its partnership with Intuition Robotics to keep deploying ElliQ, a proactive AI companion, to older residents at risk of loneliness and social isolation. The renewal is framed around three years of reported outcomes suggesting the robot can reduce loneliness and support health and wellbeing, making it a notable example of a state agency treating social robotics as part of aging-services infrastructure.

summary: The UK’s National Composites Centre will lead one-to-one business advisory support for the new £9.8 million Greater South West Robotics Adoption Hub, helping companies assess and adopt robotics and automation. summary: Counterpoint Research forecasts that DRAM demand for humanoid robot “brains” will grow 20-fold by 2030 compared with 2026, positioning robotics as a new memory growth market after AI data centers drove the HBM boom. The driver is a shift toward robot compute systems that fuse camera, LiDAR, tactile, and other sensor streams in real time for action, increasing pressure on Samsung Electronics and SK hynix to serve high-bandwidth, low-latency memory needs beyond servers.

title: Danu Robotics’ fight to build a better recycling robot
summary: Danu Robotics, founded by Amy Ma, is trying to improve recycling by building robots that can sort waste more effectively than conventional systems. The piece centers on the long, six-year push to make automated recycling sorting practical, a problem that matters because better separation of materials can raise recovery rates and reduce the amount of recyclable waste that ends up discarded.

extra.full_text: For six years, Danu founder Amy Ma has been working on a better way to sort recyclable waste.

title: IFR “한국, 제조업 로봇밀도 세계 1위…1만명당 1066대”
summary: IFR’s World Robotics 2026 report says Korea remained the world leader in manufacturing robot density in 2025, with 1,066 industrial robots per 10,000 manufacturing workers, far above the global average of 152. The gap is large enough that Korea still sits well ahead of second-place Singapore, underscoring how deeply automation is embedded in its manufacturing base even as annual growth has slowed to 2%.

title: 엔비디아, 피규어 AI에 10억달러 추가 투자 검토
summary: Nvidia is reportedly discussing an additional investment of up to $1 billion in Figure AI, the U.S. humanoid robotics company, though the deal has not been finalized and terms remain undisclosed. title: 얀 르쿤의 월드 모델 'H-제파', 단·장기 계획 분리로 로봇 경로 계획 성공률 73% 달성
summary: H-JEPA is a hierarchical world model developed by researchers including Yann LeCun that separates short-horizon, low-level motion prediction from longer-horizon abstract goal planning, rather than forcing both into one latent space. In simulated maze navigation, this split raised robot path-planning success from 18% with a single-layer model to 73%, while also reducing the computation needed for planning.

title: 印 이콘시스템즈, 최신 3D 심도카메라·AI 기반 영상 기술 공개
summary: e-con Systems showcased new AI vision cameras for mobility, humanoids, robotics, and intelligent transport systems at Vision 2026 in Stuttgart. The centerpiece was NetraVis, an active stereo 3D depth camera demonstrated on site, pointing to embedded perception hardware aimed at giving robots and autonomous systems more reliable depth sensing in real-world environments.

title: 中 노이매트릭스, 체화 세계행동모델 'Noe-0' 기술 프리뷰 공개
summary: Shanghai AI robotics company Noematrix released a technical preview of Noe-0, an embodied World Action Model trained on real-world data to help robots understand their surroundings and choose actions in physical environments. The announcement is notable because Noematrix has recently drawn attention from U.S. regulators after the Treasury sanctioned Plug and Play’s parent company, Amid LLC, for failing to report an investment in the Chinese AI robotics firm.
